# Jubilees Chapter 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Three Visitors; Sodom Destroyed; Feast of Tabernacles Ordained

---

**16:1** On the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham at the oak of Mamre, and spoke with him, and announced to him that a son would be given to him by his wife Sarah.

**16:2** Sarah laughed, for she heard us speaking these words with Abraham, and we rebuked her.

**16:3** She was afraid and denied it, saying: "I did not laugh"; for she was afraid of us.

**16:4** We told her the name of her son — as his name is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets — namely Isaac.

**16:5** When we departed from Abraham, we turned toward Sodom, and Abraham came with us to accompany us on the way.

**16:6** The LORD said: "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do, since I know that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing justice and righteousness, that the LORD may bring upon Abraham all that he has promised him?"

**16:7** "We will destroy this place for the wickedness of its inhabitants before the LORD."

**16:8** Abraham drew near and said: "Will you also destroy the righteous with the wicked? What if there are fifty righteous within the city? Will you not spare the whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are there?"

**16:9** "Far be it from you to do such a thing — to slay the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should fare as the wicked. Far be it from you. Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?"

**16:10** The LORD said: "If I find fifty righteous within the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake."

**16:11** Abraham answered: "Behold, I have ventured to speak to the LORD, though I am but dust and ashes."

**16:12** He bargained with the LORD from fifty down to ten, and the LORD said: "I will not destroy it for the sake of ten."

**16:13** We came to Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom, and when he saw us, he rose to meet us and bowed himself with his face to the ground.

**16:14** He said: "Please, my lords, turn aside to your servant's house, stay the night, wash your feet, and you may rise early and go on your way."

**16:15** They said: "No, we will spend the night in the street." But he pressed them strongly, and they turned aside to him and entered his house.

**16:16** He prepared a meal for them, baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

**16:17** Before they lay down, the men of Sodom — young and old, all the people from every quarter — surrounded the house.

**16:18** They called out to Lot: "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them."

**16:19** Lot went out to them at the door, shut the door behind him, and said: "Please, my brothers, do not act so wickedly."

**16:20** "Behold, I have two daughters who have never known a man. Let me bring them out to you; do to them as you see fit. Only do nothing to these men, for they have come under the shelter of my roof."

**16:21** They said: "Stand aside." And they said: "This fellow came to sojourn and now wants to play the judge. We will deal worse with you than with them." They pressed hard against Lot and moved to break down the door.

**16:22** The men reached out, pulled Lot back into the house, and shut the door. They struck the men at the door with blindness — great and small alike — so that they exhausted themselves trying to find the door.

**16:23** The angels said to Lot: "Have you anyone else here? Son-in-law, sons, daughters — whoever belongs to you in the city — bring them out of this place."

**16:24** "For we are about to destroy this place, because their outcry has grown great before the LORD, and the LORD has sent us to destroy it."

**16:25** Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law who had married his daughters, saying: "Get up, leave this place, for the LORD is about to destroy the city." But they thought he was joking.

**16:26** When morning came, the angels urged Lot, saying: "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, lest you be swept away in the punishment of the city."

**16:27** When he lingered, the men took hold of his hand and the hand of his wife and the hands of his two daughters — the LORD being merciful to him — and led them out, setting them down outside the city.

**16:28** When they had brought them out, one said: "Flee for your life. Do not look behind you; do not stop anywhere in the valley. Flee to the mountain, or you will be swept away."

**16:29** Then the LORD rained sulfur and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah from the LORD out of heaven.

**16:30** He overthrew those cities and all the valley and all the inhabitants of the cities and everything that grew on the ground.

**16:31** In this jubilee, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all their descendants were given the Feast of Tabernacles as an everlasting ordinance.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. Angelic first-person narration (vv.1-7) preserved. Isaac's name from the heavenly tablets (v.4) preserved as theological statement. "Know them" (v.18) retains the biblical euphemism. Feast of Tabernacles ordination (v.31) preserved as a brief but significant Jubilees calendrical claim.*
